newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Profit taking and unwinding of bear spreads made for mixed trade in CME lumber futures early, traders said.
Despite sharp gains and limit advances on Friday, futures opened easier on profit taking and lack of carryover demand. Bear spreading added to pressure in January, they said.

Although futures are at a large discount to cash, expectations are for cash markets to continue slipping from the sharp price rise posted the last couple of weeks. Demand for cash lumber had eased when recent high prices and wintry weather cut off demand, they said.
At 0933 CST, lumber ranged from $3.80 per thousand board feet lower to $5.80 higher with only January off at $400.10. March was up $1.80 at $382.50 per tbf.
